correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md uses the precise unit-rate three-opinion IPP ODE a′=c(βb−αa), b′=2αac−βb(a+c), c′=a(βb−αc), α∈(0,1), β=1−α. Direct substitution establishes mass conservation and the unique nonvertex equilibrium (β/(2−α),α/(2−α),β/(2−α)); inward-pointing faces exclude other nonvertex boundary equilibria. The relative-entropy dissipation is the sum of two nonpositive reaction terms; all three vertex neighborhoods repel an interior solution, establishing global convergence, not merely local stability. Independently sympy-reduced x=b−α/(2−α), d=c−a to x′=−βx+(2−α)x²/2−αd²/2, d′=−(λ+βx)d with λ=αβ/(2−α). Exact variation-of-constants, integrability of x and exponential bootstrap yield nonzero D=lim e^{λt}d(t) for initially asymmetric data, a forced e^{-2λt} term for α<2/3, t e^{-βt} at α=2/3, and possibly-zero C e^{-βt} for α>2/3. The correct threshold follows from β−2λ=β(2−3α)/(2−α). Finite checks corroborate but do not prove global asymptotics.
residual_risks: C at α>2/3 may vanish for exceptional data; no universal sharp lower rate there. Endpoints α=0,1, finite populations, and >3 opinions excluded. The omega-limit boundary exclusion relies on the stated compactness and Lyapunov invariance, rather than finite trajectories.
